entities.name: California State University, Long Beach
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
California State University, Long Beach (CSULB, Cal State Long Beach, founded 1949) is one of the largest universities in the California State University system (enrollment approximately 37,000 students), located in Long Beach in Los Angeles County — serving one of the most ethnically and socioeconomically diverse student populations in American higher education and recognized as one of the most diverse major universities in the United States, reflecting the extraordinary demographic complexity of the greater Los Angeles metropolitan area.

CSULB's post-WWII founding reflects the dramatic expansion of California's population during the war (workers flooding into Southern California's defense industries) and baby boom that followed. Long Beach, as home to a major port and naval base, was a center of wartime industrial activity, and the postwar population boom created urgent demand for accessible higher education. California's 1960 Master Plan for Higher Education designated Cal State institutions to provide accessible education to the broader population while reserving University of California campuses for graduate education and research.

CSULB has achieved national recognition for its diversity, educational mobility, and economic impact: it is consistently ranked as one of America's top universities for social mobility — graduating students from low-income backgrounds into middle-class professional careers. The university's enrollment of approximately 37,000 students includes a student body that is over 50% minority (majority Hispanic/Latino, Asian, and African American), making it a major institution of educational access in one of America's most diverse regions.
